To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chiral order parameter of the two-flavor QED satisfies a scaling law with the exponents {gamma}{sub +} and {beta}{sub +} of the O(4) model, and that the critical temperature is proportional to the quark mass to the power of 2/3.
the chiral order parameter in 2 flavor lattice QCD satisfies the scaling law of the O(4) spin system in 3 dimensions.

the chiral order parameter in two-flavor lattice QCD satisfies a scaling relation of the three-dimensional Heisenberg model with the critical exponent beta=0.365(5) at a temperature T=0.85T{sub c} and a quark mass m{sub {pi}}/T=0.8, where T{sub c} is the transition temperature and {pi} is the pseudoscalar meson.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the phase diagram of QCD at finite temperature and baryon density, in particular the nature of the chiral transition.
the study of the phase structure of two-flavor QMP.
the chiral phase transition of QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have found a strong indication for the existence of a second-order phase transition at T{sub c} = 0.15(2) T{sub c}(0) in the two-flavor QCP.

the chiral phase transition in 2-flavor QCD at T{sub c} {approximately} 200 MeV is a second-order transition with a nontrivial critical behavior, in the universality class of the three-dimensional Heisenberg model, with the critical exponents of the latter.
, at the present level of understanding, there is no compelling reason to believe that the QCD transition at zero baryon chemical potential is not of first order.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chiral phase transition in 2-flavor QCD at T{sub C} is of the second order in the chiral limit, but is of the first order with finite quark masses.
the lattice QCD simulation of the chiral phase transition in two-flavour QCD is consistent with the picture of the chiral transition as a second-order phase transition in the continuum limit.
the lattice data of two-flavor QMP with renormalization group-improved action are consistent with the universality hypothesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chiral order parameter of QCD with 2 flavors of quarks is consistent with the order parameter of the O(4) universality class of the 3D Ising model.
the chiral phase transition in two-flavour QCD can be understood as a second order phase transition in the continuum limit of QCD.
the scaling relation for the chiral condensation in the chiral limit is satisfied with the exponents in the 3D-Ising universality class, and the chiral transition is of second order.
